items.title: OGX Group FY26 earnings jump 51pct on stronger IT infrastructure demand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: OGX Group Bhd posted a net profit of RM3.76 million on revenue of RM58.3 million for the fourth quarter ended June 30, 2026, driven by continued growth in its information technology (IT) infrastructure solutions business. For the full financial year (FY26), net profit rose 51 per cent to RM23 million from RM15.3 million a year earlier, while revenue jumped 61 per cent to RM284.7 million from RM176 million. The group said revenue from its IT infrastructure solutions segment reached RM220 million during the year, supported by the completion of more projects.

items.title: Bursa slips ahead of Fed meeting, tech earnings
items.summary: As for the active stocks, VS Industry slipped one sen to 22 sen, SNS Network Technology and Dagang Nexchange lost two sen each to 54 sen and 43 sen respectively, Tanco added 1.5 sen to 26 sen, and Zentrix AI inched up half a sen to 69 sen. Among the top gainers, Nestle firmed RM2.36 to RM93.66, Ideal Capital jumped 25 sen to RM4, KLCC Property and REITS surged 15 sen to RM8.84, Hong Leong Bank climbed 20 sen to RM22.30, and Dutch Lady Milk Industries added 18 sen to RM32. Malaysian Pacific Industries led the top losers list, falling RM2.06 to RM44, while UMS Integration dropped 68 sen to RM7.22, Fraser & Neave lost 34 sen to RM27.50, Kelington sank 31 sen to RM7.90, and Allianz slumped 30 sen to RM21.00.

items.title: Zahid: BN staying grounded despite predictions of Negri Sembilan win
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional (BN) remains grounded despite predictions that it could secure victory in the Negri Sembilan election on Aug 1, with the coalition refusing to become overconfident. Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said BN would continue to position itself as the "underdog" to ensure its machinery and leaders remained vigilant throughout the campaign. He said maintaining an underdog mindset was crucial to ensuring the party leadership and election machinery did not overlook any group of voters or make statements that could offend the public.

items.title: Businessman: Bumi contractor’s RM1m to Bersatu was ‘reward’ after getting RM141m govt project, tapped Muhyiddin’s golf buddy’s help
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Bumiputera contractor Nepturis Sdn Bhd had given RM1 million to political party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (PPBM) in 2022 as a “reward” after the company was awarded a RM141 million government project, instead of as a “donation”, a businessman told the High Court today. Lian said he had asked Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad, whom he had heard was close to and frequently played golf with Muhyiddin, to help get Muhyiddin’s written support for Nepturis’ application for the RM141 million project. Lian, 55, said this as the 21st prosecution witness in Bersatu president and former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.

items.title: Ramanan: Locals first when hiring, foreign workers only when needed
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Malaysians must be given priority for available job opportunities before employers consider hiring foreign workers, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said. He said the policy was aligned with the Human Resources Ministry's primary objective of ensuring employment opportunities were offered to local workers first. He said the ministry would streamline the application process for foreign workers, particularly in the services sector, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's directive to expedite the recruitment of foreign labour where required.

items.title: Selangor MB Amirudin Shari orders crackdown on purported unauthorised settlements in Setia Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 28 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has ordered the local authorities to take immediate action concerning a purported illegal foreign settlement in Setia Alam. He said the directive followed a decision made at the Selangor State Security Working Committee meeting a few days ago, which stipulated that enforcement action must be taken if land encroachment is found. According to Amirudin, the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) will take action, including issuing notices to the landowners concerned and determining whether the land belongs to the government or private owners.

items.title: 113 refugees relocated after overnight police screening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All 113 Rohingya refugees who gathered outside the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in Jalan Bukit Petaling have been relocated after undergoing overnight police screening and identity verification. The refugees, who had travelled from Kampung Kuala Muda, Penang, were taken to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters in police trucks on Monday night. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said checks during the documentation and identity verification process found that all 113 individuals possessed valid UNHCR documents.

items.title: 17-year-old boy drowns after being swept away in Sungai Kampar
items.summary: The victim was identified as Amirul Danish Afizal. Perak Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call about 1.45pm before personnel from the Gopeng Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the location. He said the victim was found within 10 minutes after firefighters and members of the Fire and Rescue Academy of Malaysia (FRAM) Tronoh, who were conducting training nearby, launched a search operation.

items.title: Zahid sees 88 per cent early voting turnout as positive sign
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi described the over 88 per cent early voting turnout as a positive sign ahead of polling day on Aug 1. He said the high turnout reflected strong democratic participation and hoped the momentum would continue until polling day. "With only three days left before polling, I have instructed our election machinery to continue engaging with voters and addressing any issues they may face on polling day.

items.title: France police find five dead babies in a home
items.summary: MARSEILLE: French police have found the bodies of five babies in cardboard boxes at the home of a couple in southeast France, several sources said on Tuesday. In March, a French court jailed a 44-year-old woman for 25 years over the deaths of two of her newborn babies, who police found in the family freezer. In 2018, a court sentenced a woman with a depressive and sometimes violent husband to eight years in prison for drowning five of her newborn babies and freezing their bodies.

items.title: PPR Seri Pantai gets RM2.59m worth of upgrading works from DBKL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has allocated a total of RM2.59 million to carry out maintenance and upgrading works at the Seri Pantai People’s Housing Programme (PPR). PPR Seri Pantai, which began operating in 1998, has 936 housing units, including 615 rental units and 321 owner-occupied units. The project forms part of the federal government’s RM300 million allocation to refurbish and maintain public housing (PA) and People’s Housing Programme or Program Perumahan Rakyat (PPR) schemes managed by DBKL across Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Haunted house guide jailed for sexually assaulting 13-year-old girl
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A haunted house guide at a theme park was today sentenced to three years' jail by the Sessions Court after pleading guilty to sexually assaulting a 13-year-old girl. The court heard that Md Israful Alam, 30, a Bangladeshi, had touched the girl while she was queueing inside the haunted house at a theme park in a shopping mall. Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed the accused committing the offence while standing behind the victim.

items.title: Neutrality key to keeping Malaysia attractive to investors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: As geopolitical tensions continue to redraw the global investment map, Malaysia must remain firmly neutral to preserve its appeal as a trusted destination for foreign investors, investment and central bank leaders said. Malaysian Investment Development Authority chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz said taking sides in an increasingly fragmented world could undermine Malaysia's ability to attract investments on its own merits. He said Malaysia's neutral stance has enabled it to diversify both its trade relationships and sources of foreign direct investment, strengthening its position as an attractive investment destination.

items.title: Asean ministers voice concern over Middle East tensions, online scams
items.summary: JAKARTA: Asean foreign ministers expressed concern over escalating tensions in the Middle East and the growing threat posed by transnational online scams, calling for stronger regional cooperation, Asean Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn said on Tuesday, reported Xinhua. Speaking at the Asean Secretariat in South Jakarta, Kao said the ministers discussed geopolitical rivalry, regional security and developments in the Middle East during their annual retreat in Manila. Kao said the ministers also agreed to strengthen coordination through Asean-led security mechanisms to mitigate the impact of the conflict on Southeast Asia, particularly on energy and food security, supply chains and the safety of Asean nationals in the region.

items.title: Labourer gets six years' jail for robbery and sexual assault of foreign woman
items.summary: BESUT: A 29-year-old labourer was sentenced to a total of six years in prison and one stroke of the rotan by the Sessions Court and magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to robbing and sexually assaulting a foreign woman. Muhammad Ayub Firdaus Mohd Nor pleaded guilty to the charges after they were read out separately before Sessions Court judge Ahmad Fadhli Mahmud and magistrate Nurliyana Md Zukri. Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Akmal Mohd Jazlee prosecuted.

items.title: What are 'fire clouds', the ominous phenomenon seen in France?
items.summary: Known as "fire clouds" or pyrocumulonimbus clouds, these ominous-looking thunderstorms are created by extreme wildfires and can exacerbate already extremely dangerous conditions. What is a fire cloud? Are fire clouds rare?

items.title: Missing KK teen found safe in Inanam
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A 13-year-old student reported missing after leaving the grounds of SMK Lok Yuk in Likas on Monday has been found safe in Inanam. A family member, who declined to be identified, shared the update on social media. The girl was under police care to assist in investigations into her disappearance before being reunited with her family.

items.title: Contractor: No RM1mil Bersatu donation without Jana Wibawa project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A contractor told the High Court that his company would not have donated RM1 million to Bersatu if it had not been awarded a RM141 million Jana Wibawa project. Nepturis Sdn Bhd founder Lian Tan Chuan testified that the award followed what he described as support from then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin for the company's application to build the North Klang district police headquarters. Lian said Adam instructed him to prepare application letters seeking Muhyiddin's support for the IPD Klang Utara project.

items.title: Major quake in southern Japan knocks out power, disrupts transport
items.summary: TOKYO: An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.1 struck Japan's southern Kumamoto prefecture on Tuesday, knocking out power to thousands of homes, snarling travel and triggering evacuation orders and warnings for aftershocks. Speaking to reporters at her office in Tokyo, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the extent of casualties and property damage was being assessed. "We have already been informed that people have been injured," Takaichi said.

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls: Johari urges Malay leaders to reject racial political narratives
items.summary: JEMPOL: Malay leaders must not be trapped by racial political narratives but instead must take responsibility for safeguarding the interests of all communities in the country, said Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He said Malaysia was built as a multiracial nation, with Malays forming the majority population. Although Umno is a Malay-based party, he said BN has remained a multiracial coalition representing Malaysian society since its formation.

items.title: Bar warns Admiralty Jurisdiction Bill falls short of global standards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Bar has voiced its disappointment over the newly introduced Admiralty Jurisdiction Bill 2026, saying the proposed legislation falls short of international benchmarks. The Bar also said it could undermine the nation's ambition to become a leading regional maritime hub. Bar president Anand Raj said the draft legislation failed to meaningfully incorporate recommendations developed through years of extensive stakeholder consultations.

items.title: Massachusetts mother goes on trial for killing her three children
items.summary: DUXBURY: A Massachusetts jury heard dueling accounts on Monday for why a mother killed her three young children in 2023, a tragedy that a defense lawyer said was due to her suffering from postpartum mental illness and that a prosecutor called a planned murder. During his opening statement in Plymouth County Superior Court, defence attorney Kevin Reddington told jurors that Clancy, now 35, had struggled for months with postpartum mental health issues following the birth of her third child. "She's living her own hell," he said.

items.title: Former unit trust consultant jailed 18 months, fined RM2m for investment fraud
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — A former unit trust consultant was sentenced to 18 months in prison and fined a total of RM2 million by two Sessions Courts here today after pleading guilty to cheating two men in connection with investments in securities. Judge Azrul Darus sentenced Amran Mohd Amin, 59, to 18 months in prison and a fine of RM1 million, or six months’ imprisonment in default, for the first charge. However, the two prison terms will run concurrently from the date of Amran’s arrest on September 8, 2025.

items.title: After nearly three years, Johor police reclassify baby’s death as murder, father named main suspect
items.summary: The probe also identified the 18-month-old victim’s father as the main suspect. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said a report on the case was received from a doctor attached to the Sultan Ismail Hospital’s (HSI) emergency department here on September 13, 2023. He said the victim, who was unconscious, was brought to the hospital by his 40-year-old father.

items.title: World risks HIV resurgence as funding falls 18 per cent: UNAIDS
items.summary: GENEVA: The world risks a resurgence of the HIV epidemic after global funding fell by nearly a fifth last year, the UN body fighting AIDS said on Monday. Washington previously accounted for 75 per cent of international HIV funding before President Donald Trump's return to the White House in January 2025. Some 1.2 million people caught HIV last year.

items.title: Bahrain to cover F1 rights fees for Sepang race, says SIC
items.summary: SEPANG, July 28 — Bahrain will fully bear the Formula One (F1) rights fees of US$70 million (RM298 million) to US$80 million for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, according to SIC. SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said this arrangement was agreed through cooperation between SIC and the Bahrain International Circuit (BIC). However, Azhan Shafriman said Malaysia still needs to share the cost of local preparations of around RM40 million to ensure the circuit meets Formula One specifications.

items.title: Azalina: Local candidates better placed to address community issues
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Local candidates are better placed to understand and address community issues, making them the ideal choice in the Negri Sembilan elections, said Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said BN's candidate for the constituency would secure a convincing victory, citing encouraging feedback received during engagements with voters. On BN's strategy to engage young voters, she said the coalition had long prioritised youth outreach through Umno Youth and Puteri Umno, well before the implementation of the Undi18 initiative.

items.title: Transport Ministry says Putrajaya monorail project not viable to revive
items.summary: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) in a written response posted on the Parliament website today said the findings were obtained through the Public Transport Study in Putrajaya, Cyberjaya, Bangi and Kajang which also assessed the feasibility of the monorail system. Alternatively, the ministry said that the Nadi Putra Bus service currently involves seven routes with 26 buses and records an average of 2,246 passengers on weekdays. The shuttle bus service includes two routes with eight buses and an average of 1,173 passengers, while the Rapid On-Demand involves three routes with nine vans and an average of 315 passengers on weekdays.

items.title: Government allocates RM1.7 billion to replace ageing water pipes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The federal government has approved an allocation of RM1.7 billion under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) to replace about 1,800km of critical water pipes nationwide between 2026 and 2030. Deputy Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Rahman Mohamad said the programme would prioritise the replacement of ageing asbestos-cement (AC) pipes and other critical pipelines that have exceeded their design lifespan to reduce the country's Non-Revenue Water (NRW) rate. He was responding to a question from Senator Datuk Wu Him Ven on the government's action plan for replacing asbestos-cement water pipes.

items.title: Malaysia registers 26 rare disease medicines since 2020, says Health Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — A total of 26 medicines for rare diseases had been registered in Malaysia as of April this year, from none before 2020, the Dewan Negara was told today. Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib said the milestone reflects the Ministry of Health's (MOH) ongoing efforts to improve access to medicines and treatment for patients with rare diseases. Hanifah Hajar said 529 types of rare diseases have been identified and included in the Malaysian Rare Disease List, with about 80 per cent attributed to genetic factors.

items.title: 113 Rohingya refugees moved to NGO-designated location from KL police headquarters
items.summary: City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the group departed from the police headquarters about 4pm. "The group included refugees aged between one month and 60 years old," he said. The group comprised 110 Rohingya refugees, one Iraqi man, one Somali woman and one Indonesian woman married to a Rohingya refugee.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for KL, parts of Selangor, Johor, Sarawak and three states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several areas across the country, including parts of Perlis, Kedah, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Johor and Sarawak. The areas involved are Perlis; Kedah districts of Langkawi, Kubang Pasu and Kota Setar; Selangor districts of Gombak and Hulu Langat; Kuala Lumpur; Negeri Sembilan’s Jelebu; Johor districts of Mersing, Kulai, Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru; and Kuching, Sarawak. The warning was issued at 4pm today.

items.title: Six brothers charged with trafficking 118g of heroin in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH, July 28 — Six siblings were charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with trafficking 118.87 grams of heroin last week. Muhammad Affandi Zulkafli, 41, Muhammad Khairul Azmil Zulkafli, 40, Shahrul Azwan Zulkafli, 38, Mohamad Shah Herman Zulkafli, 35, Muhamad Amirul Zulkafli, 29, and Mohamad Hafizi Zulkafli, 27, all unemployed, nodded after the charge was read out before Magistrate Norizan Riduan. According to the charge, the six brothers allegedly trafficked 118.87 grams of heroin at an unnumbered hut beside a house along Laluan Usaha, Kampung Che Zainal Tambahan 1, Chemor, at about 9.20pm on July 21.

items.title: Negri Sembilan police deny claims personnel were bribed to vote
items.summary: NILAI: Negri Sembilan police have denied allegations by Parti Wawasan Negara coordinator Badrul Hisham Shaharin, better known as Chegubard, that police personnel were bribed to vote for a particular political party. State police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said an investigation would be carried out if a police report was lodged over the allegations. "If a police report is lodged, we will conduct an investigation.

items.title: Family shaken after firecrackers allegedly thrown at Kelantan house
items.summary: District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Azmir Damiri confirmed that police had received a report on the incident, adding that no suspect had been arrested so far. The incident occurred at about 1.15am when 30-year-old Nur Shairah Solehah Ahmad Norzaki, a mother of three, had just returned from work. [[nid:1498976]] She said eight family members were inside the house during the incident, including her mother, three siblings and her three children, the youngest aged three.

items.title: Keiko Fujimori set to take office as Peru president
items.summary: LIMA: Peru's right-wing president-elect Keiko Fujimori will take office on Tuesday, vowing to tackle the wave of crime sweeping the Andean nation. Fujimori won the June 7 presidential runoff by fewer than 50,000 votes, after losing the past three runoffs. The 51-year-old came head-to-head with leftist Roberto Sanchez, with her campaign shadowed by the divisive legacy of her father Alberto Fujimori, who ruled Peru in the 1990s.

items.title: Police: All Rohingya refugees relocated to KL headquarters hold valid UNHCR documents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — All the 110 Rohingya refugees relocated to the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters (IPK) yesterday possess valid documents issued by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), according to police. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the verification was made following screening and documentation processes conducted on the group of refugees at Dataran Wira within the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters. “During the relocation at about 8.50pm, a total of 110 Rohingya refugees, along with three other foreign nationals, were transferred to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters with the cooperation of UNHCR.

items.title: Felda settler killed in Jempol crash with lorry after motorcycle enters opposite lane
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — A Felda settler was killed after the motorcycle he was riding entered the opposite lane and collided with a lorry along Kilometer 18 of Jalan Bahau-Kemayan in Jempol, Negeri Sembilan, this morning. Jempol district police chief Superintendent Norhisham Mustapar said the crash at about 11.25am involved a Hino lorry driven by a 53-year-old man travelling from Bahau towards Triang, Pahang, and a Honda C100 motorcycle ridden by the 73-year-old victim, Kosmo! “Upon reaching the scene, as the lorry driver was travelling straight, the victim’s motorcycle from the opposite direction suddenly entered the lorry’s path, causing a collision involving the front right side of the lorry.

items.title: Ex-unit trust consultant jailed, fined RM2mil for investment scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A former unit trust consultant was sentenced to 18 months' jail and fined RM2 million by two Sessions Courts after pleading guilty to cheating two men in a securities investment scam. Amran Mohd Amin, 59, received an 18-month jail sentence and a RM1 million fine from Sessions Court judge Azrul Darus for one charge. The jail terms will run concurrently from Amran's arrest on Sept 8 last year.

items.title: Recognising the majority who protect our communities
items.summary: LETTERS: The recent news of several policemen being detained over an extortion case has understandably drawn public attention and raised questions. Day in and day out, they work to maintain public order, protect our communities, fight criminal activity and keep our streets safe. Allegations of extortion — especially when foreign nationals are among the victims — strike at the very heart of public trust in our law enforcement system.

items.title: Sarawak crocodile sighting near Sibu flyover sparks public warning
items.summary: SIBU, July 28 — The sight of a crocodile lurking in a pond near the Jalan Oya-Sibu Jaya flyover has prompted a warning for the public on social media. Licensed crocodile hunter Jeferry Siew shared a video of the sighting on a Facebook post, which warned those who frequented the pond for recreational fishing to always exercise caution. In the clip, Siew expressed concern that the crocodile might have been deliberately released into the pond.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polls: EC targets voter turnout of 75pc on Saturday
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — The Election Commission (EC) is targeting a voter turnout of between 72 and 75 per cent for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election this Saturday, its chairman, Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun, said. As of 10am, early voter turnout stood at 34.26 per cent. He said the number of eligible early voters had been revised from 22,339 to 16,467 after some voters who initially applied for early voting opted to vote by post instead.

items.title: Family of teen killed in drug-fuelled Teluk Intan crash seeks justice
items.summary: IPOH: The family of one of two teenage girls killed in a crash in Teluk Intan on Sunday wants the driver involved to face the full force of the law after he tested positive for drugs. The victim's cousin, Afrina Wardina Syamimi Azlizam, 16, said the parents of Nur Atikah Abdullah hope the driver will be held accountable for the death of their youngest child. Afrina said the last time she communicated with Nur Atikah was on the victim's birthday on July 18 via WhatsApp.

items.title: Migrant worker abuse a national security risk: Analyst
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Abuse of Malaysia's migrant worker recruitment ecosystem should no longer be treated solely as a labour or human trafficking issue, but as a national security concern. Saying this, security and defence analyst Zaki Salleh said the recruitment of foreign workers far beyond actual industry demand could create risks extending well beyond labour market distortions. "When there are significantly more migrant workers entering the country than available employment opportunities, the implications extend far beyond illegal employment.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan early voter turnout tops 80pc at 2pm as 20 centres close
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — Two more early polling centres for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, involving security force personnel and their spouses, closed at 2pm today. Earlier, 18 early polling centres closed at noon, while the remaining 18 centres will close at 5pm this evening. Early voting involves 22,339 registered voters.

items.title: No land will be acquired for Port Dickson Smart Port, says Aminuddin
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — The AI-powered Smart Port project in Port Dickson will be developed entirely on land owned by Tanco Holdings Berhad and its subsidiary, Midports Holdings Sdn Bhd, without the need to acquire any additional land, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said. He dismissed allegations that the project would involve the acquisition of about 566 hectares (1,400 acres) of land, including village areas, forest reserves, customary land, industrial zones, agricultural land, and residential lots, describing the claims as baseless. Furthermore, there is no customary land in Port Dickson.

items.title: Maritime executive says K8 declaration confusion affecting industry, urges Customs Dept to clarify
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy today urged the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) to provide an immediate explanation on the implementation of the K8 declaration procedure, claiming confusion over its application is affecting petroleum industry operations at Tanjung Langsat Port. He said clarification was needed to ensure industry players clearly understood the interpretation and implementation of the K8 procedure, particularly in relation to the handling of petroleum cargo after it has been unloaded into storage tanks. He also sought clarification on Customs' monitoring procedures after cargo is unloaded into storage tanks, the traceability mechanism linking documentation with the physical cargo, and the procedures to ensure exported cargo corresponds with the original declaration.

items.title: Malaysia eyes new framework to deal with economic crisis risks, says PM’s adviser
items.summary: KUALA LIMPUR, July 28 — The government is looking to establish an economic security framework to strengthen the country's resilience against future crises, says the economic adviser to the Prime Minister's Office Nurhisham Hussein. Themed “Reforms for Resilience: Navigating Uncertainties”, the SS2026, held from July 28-29, features discussions on key economic and financial issues, including economic resilience, wages, cost of living challenges, investments, energy security, Islamic finance and private healthcare costs. Meanwhile, Nurhisham said the government is also actively looking at how Malaysia can attract investments and benefit from the global disruptions.

items.title: Deputy minister: Govt studies new data centre projects to prevent strain on power, water supplies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — All applications for new data centre projects undergo strict assessments to ensure electricity and water supplies to households and local industries are not affected, Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said today. “The government is always careful when approving applications related to data centres,” he said during question time in the Dewan Negara. He said the government had also organised matching programmes between multinational corporations and local companies to help small and medium enterprises become suppliers.

items.title: Govt to launch digital trust strategy, enforcement framework by year-end, says Gobind
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The Digital Ministry is drafting a comprehensive strategy centred on building trust in emerging technologies, with a targeted rollout by the end of this year, said Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo. Gobind explained that the strategy was originally slated for an earlier release but was rescheduled to prioritise the launch of the national AI Malaysia (AIM) platform. “It also comes back now to us building trust.

items.title: Johor police bust two scam rings operating in Forest City, 335 suspects nabbed
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, July 28 — Johor police have busted two online scam syndicates that operate call centres in Forest City in Iskandar Puteri, following the arrest of 335 suspects that included foreigners recently. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspects were nabbed in an integrated operation carried out simultaneously on 27 residential apartment units and five bungalows which were used as the syndicate’s operations centre. Also present was deputy Johor police chief Hoo Chuan Huat and senior officers.

items.title: Strong demand for Malaysia’s US$1.5b sukuk signals investor confidence, says Bank Negara governor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Malaysia’s successful US$1.5 billion (RM6.13 billion) global sukuk issuance last week shows investors’ confidence in its economic fundamentals, said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour. “Investors were not only willing to commit capital to Malaysia. Creating higher-skilled jobs at scale takes time,” he said.

items.title: Menara Merdeka 118 officially renamed Menara Merdeka Maybank; former HQ now Menara Tun Perak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Menara Merdeka 118 has officially been renamed Menara Merdeka Maybank, reflecting Maybank’s presence at the landmark building that now serves as the group’s headquarters. Maybank said the new registered address of its headquarters is Level 70, Menara Merdeka Maybank, Presint Merdeka 118, 50118 Kuala Lumpur, effective today. The banking group also announced that its former headquarters at Jalan Tun Perak, previously known as Menara Maybank, has been renamed Menara Tun Perak from today.

items.title: Company’s RM19.5m donation to Bersatu was due to project award after Muhyiddin’s minutes, MD says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Construction company Mamfor Sdn Bhd’s managing director Shahradzi Shamsuddin said his firm had donated RM19.5 million to Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia in 2021 and 2022, as he viewed the RM605.2 million government project awarded to his younger brother’s company Sutracom Sdn Bhd as being due to then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s 2021 minutes. Shahradzi’s brother’s company Sutracom was eventually awarded the project in October 2022. Shahradzi’s company’s Mamfor’s RM19.5 million donation to Bersatu was done in stages, namely RM10.5 million and RM9 million before and after the project was awarded.

items.title: Malaysia has enough fuel supply until year-end, govt securing 2027 stocks, says economy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Malaysia has begun securing fuel supplies for next year as the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz shows no signs of ending, with the government saying it has already ensured sufficient supply through the end of this year. He said Malaysia has managed to secure fuel supplies until the end of the year through mitigation measures and is now focused on ensuring supplies remain stable into next year. “We have managed to secure the fuel supply until year’s end, and we also have to try to secure supply for the coming year,” he said.

items.title: High Court orders Malaysian govt, police to pay activists RM195,000 over unlawful 2021 vigil arrests
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The High Court today ordered the government and police to pay RM195,000 in damages to 13 activists after finding their arrests during a candlelight vigil for Covid-19 victims in 2021 were unlawful. Free Malaysia Today reported that Justice Datuk Anand Ponnudurai awarded each of the activists RM15,000 after holding the police officers involved and the government liable for the arrests made following the August 19, 2021 gathering at Dataran Merdeka. In his judgment, Anand said the activists were effectively deprived of their freedom after police seized their identity cards at the scene and directed them to go to the Dang Wangi police headquarters despite the gathering having ended.

items.title: Komtar tourist attraction cleared to continue operations after fatal fall, says Penang CM
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 28 — The operator of a tourist attraction in Komtar has been allowed to continue operating after the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) confirmed it had complied with all required safety measures following an incident involving an 18-year-old last weekend. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said JBPM had verified that the operator met all safety requirements and found no reason to halt operations. “The Fire and Rescue Department has confirmed that the operating company complied with all the required safety measures and has been allowed to continue operating,” he told reporters today after visiting a factory in Bayan Lepas.

items.title: Most infrastructure ready ahead of 2027 dual Year One intake, says education minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 28 — The majority of infrastructure projects to support the intake of six-year-old Year One pupils for the 2027 school session have been completed ahead of schedule, Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said. Fadhlina said the ministry is also making comprehensive preparations for teacher placement and other operational requirements based on projected student enrolment to ensure a smooth transition for the dual Year One intake. However, she noted that the ministry continues to receive inquiries and registration applications from parents even as planning for next year’s school session enters its final stage.

items.title: Form Six transfer to Higher Education Ministry put on hold, says Anwar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 28 — The current pre-university management system for Form Six students will continue to be overseen by the Ministry of Education (MOE) for the time being, to ensure the smooth operation of the existing framework, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Elaborating further, the Prime Minister said that although Sixth Form remains under MOE, its students must have a distinct identity as post-secondary and pre-university learners. For example, Sixth Form students should not be included in general school assemblies.

items.title: MACC pursues documents from Dubai, Singapore and Indonesia as KWAP investment probe widens
items.summary: MELAKA, July 28 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has identified Dubai, Singapore and Indonesia as the three key jurisdictions from which it intends to obtain documents through the Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) process as part of its investigation into investment activities involving the Retirement Fund (Incorporated) (KWAP). MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the commission is working with the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) to initiate the MLA process after determining that key documents related to the investments are believed to be located overseas. Since then, he said the MACC has recorded statements from 20 witnesses, including KWAP and MOF officials, members of KWAP’s Investment Committee, and investment panel members.
